about: The package's own Linux inputs: a copy of Lane G's pack-inputs.json (oshal-handover lanes/linux-application-packs-2026-11-13/pack-inputs.json, last updated 2026-11-13T17:33:12Z by lane-g3-linux-any-program), with Lane G4's wording for the programs Orbit now starts readable (kernel 6602c84d); the programs named in `amended` are the only ones that differ from Lane G's file, and tests/sheet/linux-sources.test.cjs holds that. Lane G's own description follows. Step D of the Linux application packs (Lane G, 2026-11-13): what the generated instructions for three Linux programs must say and must not say, as input for Lane A's writer package program-instructions. Every fact is as built at kernel commit 1cefa139 on dev/native-parity (Writer's replace-text and find-replace facts updated by Lane G2, with and without the add-on; the rest as Lane G wrote them at 33ec9e1b) and names the test that proves it on the real program (scripts/test-linux-apps-desktop.cjs in the private desktop of linux-apps-desktop.Dockerfile, unless another file is named). The verbs, inputs and refusal words of each bridge word are in bridge-facts.json beside this file. `acceptance` is a check a written pack can be held to: `contains` are phrases it must hold, `absent` are phrases it must not.

contract.note: The kernel's own contract for every pack (T76 proposal 4.3 and validate_body): at most the two tools, only the actions listed, 200 to 8,192 bytes, first line starting with '# ', no address and no tool_call or handoff block.

amended.what: Lane G4 (kernel 6602c84d): when Orbit opens Chrome or VS Code it adds --force-renderer-accessibility, and Firefox or Thunderbird it starts with GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY=1, for that one process; a copy the person started unreadable is refused as "it was started without accessibility; close it and let Jarvis open it, or use the mouse and keyboard.". Each program's first fact says so with G4's proof, Firefox's and Thunderbird's second fact reads "Started readable" for "With the switch on", a never-line says the person changes no setting, and 'started without accessibility' is a required word (for Firefox and Thunderbird in place of 'accessibility switch').

programs.name: Text Editor (GNOME Text Editor)

must_say.fact: Text Editor edits plain text files. `computer.open` with app org.gnome.texteditor starts it; `computer.app` with "action": "apps" lists its open windows.
must_say.evidence: bound-apps.ts openIfBound; test D6 and D7 (apps names the bridge accessibility)

must_say.fact: A snapshot holds the whole document as one element with the role text box, editable, whose value is the document's text.
must_say.evidence: deca2148, test 'D6 and D7: Text Editor's window (published as an application) is found, and its document (a text box) is read and editable'

must_say.fact: To change the document, type into that element: mode replace sets the whole text, insert puts the text at `at`, append adds it at the end.
must_say.evidence: 1bbde785, test 'D1 and D2: a type into Text Editor answers what was read back, with verified ...'; measure-after-c/measure.json text-editor probes (append, two-line replace, write-back, 3 of 3)

must_say.fact: The answer's `after` is what the document holds when read again, and `verified` says whether that is what was asked for. When verified is false, read a new snapshot before anything else; do not repeat the type.
must_say.evidence: 1bbde785, same test; bridges/atspi.ts writeText

must_say.fact: A change is undone with "action": "undo", which writes the earlier text back only while the document still holds what was written; otherwise "action": "restore" opens the copy saved before it.
must_say.evidence: same test (the undo answers the earlier text, verified); app-acts.ts undo

must_say.fact: Text Editor declares no verbs: opening, saving, searching and replacing files are not done through invoke, which answers "I can't do <verb> in Text Editor yet." The person saves the file in Text Editor.
must_say.evidence: bridges/linux-apps.ts declared (verbs only for a LibreOffice text document); app-control.ts invoke

must_say.fact: A one-line box in Text Editor (such as its search box) is not typed into: "Orbit cannot tell whether this box is a password field, so it does not type into it".
must_say.evidence: deca2148, test 'D3: a one-line GTK 4 text box is refused ...'

must_not_say: A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (no Ctrl+S, no File menu).
That Jarvis saves, opens or searches files in Text Editor.
Any declared verb for Text Editor (insert-paragraph, format-text, save-document and the rest belong to LibreOffice).
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

programs.name: Terminal (GNOME Terminal)

must_say.fact: `computer.open` with app org.gnome.terminal opens a Terminal window; `computer.app` with "action": "apps" lists its windows.
must_say.evidence: bound-apps.ts openIfBound; test D4 (bound from Open now)

must_say.fact: A snapshot reads the lines shown in the terminal as one element with the role terminal; the empty rows below the last line are empty lines. Only what is shown is read.
must_say.evidence: cf94cdb4, test 'D4: a terminal's lines are read, and typing into it is refused ...'; measure-after-c/measure.json terminal

must_say.fact: Nothing is typed into the terminal: "action": "type" is refused with "Terminal did not do that: This needs the mouse and keyboard." and nothing reaches the program running in it. Do not repeat it; tell the person the terminal takes typing only from the keyboard.
must_say.evidence: cf94cdb4, same test (a fresh snapshot shows nothing reached the program)

must_say.fact: Terminal declares no verbs; invoke answers "I can't do <verb> in Terminal yet."
must_say.evidence: bridges/linux-apps.ts declared; app-control.ts invoke

must_not_say: A command for Jarvis to type into the terminal, or any shell command presented as something Jarvis runs there.
A key or key combination as something Jarvis does.
That the terminal's text can be changed through computer.app.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

programs.name: LibreOffice Writer
programs.shipped_guide: platform/docs/guides/libreoffice-writer.md (Lane A's decision 9: the shipped guide comes first and the pack after it; the pack adds and must not contradict it)

must_say.fact: Two ways in, told apart by the snapshot: with Orbit's LibreOffice add-on connected, `part` is "whole" and the reading holds every paragraph and table; without it, `part` is "visible" and `shown` says "the paragraphs shown on the screen".
must_say.evidence: bridges/libreoffice.ts read; bridges/atspi.ts readTextDocument; test-attached-apps-desktop.cjs (visible part) and test-libreoffice-plugin-desktop.cjs (whole document)

must_say.fact: With the add-on: the declared verbs insert-paragraph, add-section, replace-text, delete-paragraph, format-text, find-replace and the file verbs recent-documents, open-document, new-document, save-document, export-document, each through "action": "invoke", each one step on LibreOffice's own Undo.
must_say.evidence: bridge-facts.json bridges.libreoffice.declared.text; test-libreoffice-plugin-desktop.cjs

must_say.fact: With the add-on (1.2.3 and later), replace-text and find-replace change only the matched text, as without it: the text around it keeps its bold, italic and font, the new text takes the formatting of the text it replaces, a match in more than one formatting is refused and nothing changes, and the answer carries `verified` from reading back the text and each character's formatting. find-replace with the add-on reaches the whole document (tables left out), and `"all": false` changes only the first match; the whole change is one named step on LibreOffice's Undo. A line ending in the new text is a line break inside that paragraph, with or without the add-on; add paragraphs with insert-paragraph.
must_say.evidence: 1cefa139, scripts/test-libreoffice-plugin-desktop.cjs tests 'G2 with the add-on: replace-text changes only the matched word ...', '... replace-text on the bold word gives its bold to the new word ...', '... find-replace changes the word in both paragraphs ...', '... a line ending in the new text is a line break ...', '... a match across a change of formatting is refused ...' (red on add-on 1.2.2, green on 1.2.3: lane-g2/addon-red-before and lane-g2/addon-green)

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: insert-paragraph and add-section add plain paragraphs only; a heading, a font size, or bold, italic or underline inside insert-paragraph or replace-text is refused in words naming the add-on ("... needs the LibreOffice add-on: install it in Orbit Settings, Bound Apps (Install the LibreOffice add-on)"), and nothing changes.
must_say.evidence: d19e4be8, tests 'D2, Writer over the bus: insert-paragraph adds a paragraph ...' and '... a heading is refused in words naming the add-on, and nothing changes'

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: format-text sets bold, italic or underline on a paragraph (`ref`) or a text (`find`) and is checked in the text's own attributes; when the format does not read back it is refused and nothing is claimed.
must_say.evidence: d19e4be8, test 'D2, Writer over the bus: format-text makes the word bold, checked in its own attributes, and one Undo takes it away'

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: replace-text (with `find`) and find-replace change only the matched text. The text around it keeps its bold, italic and font, and the new text takes the formatting of the text it replaces (a bold word replaced stays bold). The answer's `verified` is true only when both the text and that formatting read back as expected.
must_say.evidence: 8c2ac754, scripts/test-linux-apps-desktop.cjs tests 'G2, Writer over the bus: replace-text changes only the matched word; ...', '... replace-text on the bold word gives its bold to the new word ...', '... find-replace changes the word in both paragraphs ...' (red at edee33a5, green at 8c2ac754: lane-g2/red-before and lane-g2/green-after)

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: a match that is in more than one formatting (part bold, part plain) is refused and nothing changes: "'<text>' is in more than one formatting ('<part>' | '<part>'), so its new text could keep only one of them; nothing changed. Replace each part on its own." Replace each part with its own replace-text.
must_say.evidence: 8c2ac754, test 'G2, Writer over the bus: a match that crosses a change of formatting is refused before anything changes'; bridge-facts.json bridges.linux-atspi declared replace-text and find-replace refuses

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: replace-text without `find` replaces the paragraph's whole text (by `ref`, else the first paragraph shown); the new text takes the formatting the paragraph ends with. With a `find` the paragraph named by `ref` does not hold, it is refused and nothing changes.
must_say.evidence: 8c2ac754, test 'G2, Writer over the bus: a whole-paragraph replace-text (no find) changes that paragraph only, and one Undo puts its bold back'; bridges/linux-writer.ts replaceText

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: find-replace reaches only the paragraphs shown on the screen, changes at most 10 places at once (20 when the replacement is empty), is refused when the paragraphs shown hold none, and answers the touched paragraphs before and as read back. One "action": "undo" with its group takes the whole change away. Searching the whole document in one step needs the add-on.
must_say.evidence: 8c2ac754, test 'G2, Writer over the bus: find-replace changes the word in both paragraphs ...' and 'G2: one find-replace over the bus changes at most ten places ...'; bridges/linux-writer.ts placesRefusal

must_say.fact: Without the add-on: delete-paragraph leaves the paragraph empty in place; the file verbs are refused.
must_say.evidence: bridges/linux-writer.ts clearParagraph; bridge-facts.json bridges.linux-atspi.writer_over_the_bus

must_say.fact: Every edit's answer carries `after` as read back and `verified`; when verified is false, read a new snapshot before anything else.
must_say.evidence: d19e4be8 and 1bbde785, the Writer and Text Editor tests

must_say.fact: An edit is undone with "action": "undo" naming the answer's undo `how` and `group`.
must_say.evidence: d19e4be8 (one Undo removes the inserted paragraph and the bold); test-attached-edits-desktop.cjs

must_not_say: That a heading, a font size or a paragraph style can be set without the add-on.
That replace-text or find-replace drop the formatting of the paragraph they change, with or without the add-on (both did in Orbit 0.7.19 with add-on 1.2.2; since kernel 1cefa139 neither does).
A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does (the shipped guide names menus only as where the person finds things).
Anything the shipped guide says differently about the add-on's verbs.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

programs.name: Google Chrome

must_say.fact: Chrome shows what is inside its window to computer.app only when it was started with --force-renderer-accessibility, and Orbit adds that flag itself when it opens Chrome with computer.open (by its bound key, with a file, or by its program name). A Chrome the person started without it is refused in words: "Orbit cannot read Google Chrome's controls: it was started without accessibility; close it and let Jarvis open it, or use the mouse and keyboard." Ask the person to close Chrome and open it again with computer.open, or the page is done by mouse and keyboard.
must_say.evidence: 6602c84d (Lane G4), desktop/oshal-node/scripts/test-linux-open-readable.cjs 'Chrome already running as the person started it (no flag)...', 'Chrome closed, then opened by Orbit with a file...' and 'app.open with a program name that is not bound ("google-chrome"...'; test-linux-any-program.cjs 'Chrome as it starts by default publishes an empty window...' (refused as started without accessibility since 6602c84d); src/main/readable-launch.ts STARTED_UNREADABLE

must_say.fact: With the flag, a snapshot reads the page shown: headings, paragraphs, field labels and values, buttons, check boxes, list boxes, and the tab and address bar.
must_say.evidence: c0d3cb39, test-linux-any-program.cjs 'Chrome with --force-renderer-accessibility...'

must_say.fact: "action": "press" presses a button or check box on the page. Nothing can be typed into a field or the address bar through computer.app: a type is refused "This needs the mouse and keyboard."
must_say.evidence: c0d3cb39, test-linux-any-program.cjs 'Chrome with --force-renderer-accessibility...'

must_say.fact: A list box cannot be chosen from ("that element cannot be selected"), a password field is never typed into, and scroll is refused because Chrome publishes no scroll bar.
must_say.evidence: c0d3cb39, test-linux-any-program.cjs 'Chrome: a list box that cannot be selected...'; probes/results chrome-force (scroll)

must_say.fact: Act only in a Chrome window that is in front: a window covered by another runs no press and does not update what it shows until it is uncovered.
must_say.evidence: lane-g3/probes/chrome-press.cjs covered: "Not pressed" for 3 s after a press

must_not_say: That the person must start Chrome with a flag or change a desktop setting: Orbit starts it readable when it opens it.
That Jarvis types into a page field, the address bar or a search box in Chrome.
That Jarvis chooses an option in a list box.
A menu path, a key or a key combination as something Jarvis does.
Any tool other than computer.app and computer.open.

Eleven Linux document programs measured on the Spark (kernel c0d3cb39 Orbit bridge, 6e05f160 PROGRAMS): google-chrome, firefox, thunderbird, com.microsoft.vscode, org.xfce.mousepad, org.gnome.evince, org.gnome.nautilus, thunar, org.kde.okular, org.gnome.eog, xfce4-terminal; each fact names its test in desktop/oshal-node/scripts/test-linux-any-program.cjs or its probe in lane-g3/probes. The measured per-program record is lane-g3/programs.json, also embedded in bridge-facts.json.

Lane G4 (kernel 6602c84d): when Orbit opens Chrome or VS Code it adds --force-renderer-accessibility, and Firefox or Thunderbird it starts with GNOME_ACCESSIBILITY=1, for that one process; a copy the person started unreadable is refused as "it was started without accessibility; close it and let Jarvis open it, or use the mouse and keyboard.". Each program's first fact says so with G4's proof, Firefox's and Thunderbird's second fact reads "Started readable" for "With the switch on", a never-line says the person changes no setting, and 'started without accessibility' is a required word (for Firefox and Thunderbird in place of 'accessibility switch').

Lane LX1 (kernel 4eb54fdb): nineteen everyday Linux programs measured on the Spark in test-linux-everyday-programs.cjs (gedit, Calculator, To Do, Document Scanner, Calendar, Characters, Transmission, File Roller, PDF Arranger, System Monitor, Fonts, Videos, Rhythmbox, Shotwell, Ristretto, Remmina, qBittorrent, Claude, ChatGPT), each with what Jarvis reads, does and is refused; qBittorrent, Claude and ChatGPT are started readable by Orbit's computer.open.
